ns1:item.ns1:title: Economic-boom-driven electricity demand linked to urban air pollution and health in India
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Cities, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00518-9

Rapid economic growth in India since 2000 has increased electricity demand, with most of the electricity generated from coal. This study finds that rising sulfur dioxide emissions and sulfate aerosol pollution increased mortality attributable to PM2.5, whereas cleaner cooking fuels reduced household air pollution.
ns1:item.dc:title: Economic-boom-driven electricity demand linked to urban air pollution and health in India

ns1:item.ns1:title: Urban trees associated with a reduction in negative sentiment with stronger links during COVID-19
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Cities, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00519-8

Urban tree canopy significantly mitigates negative sentiment on social media, with effects amplified during COVID-19. Utilizing high-resolution satellite imagery and geotagged social media data, fixed-effects models reveal optimal canopy coverage thresholds for emotional well-being.
ns1:item.dc:title: Urban trees associated with a reduction in negative sentiment with stronger links during COVID-19
ns1:item.dc:creator: Jianhua Guo
Huadong Guo
Jianghao Wang
Danfeng Hong
Anna Kruspe
Xiao Xiang Zhu

ns1:item.ns1:title: Sustaining green stormwater infrastructure adoption in cities
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Cities, Published online: 21 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00520-1

Widespread adoption of green stormwater infrastructure is critical for realizing citywide stormwater resilience, but adoption remains highly uneven. The study shows how neighborhood visibility, conversion capacity and social capital interact to drive or constrain widespread uptake.
ns1:item.dc:title: Sustaining green stormwater infrastructure adoption in cities
ns1:item.dc:creator: Koorosh Azizi
Margaret Garcia
Dev Niyogi
R. Patrick Bixler
